intent: Looped slow-run cycle with two functionally symmetric half-strides: the legs alternate forward and backward, the pelvis bobs vertically with a small lateral shift, and the torso and arms counter-rotate with the running rhythm.

phases.description: Stride A with pelvis rise from the loop baseline to the first stride extreme; the pelvis reaches its highest point at f5.
Recovery with pelvis lowering; the body passes through recovery while the pelvis shifts laterally to its leftmost point at f11.
Stride B with pelvis rise in the opposite half-stride; several shoulder and leg rotation extrema cluster around f15-f16.
Recovery and loop return; the pelvis continues lowering and shifting right before returning near the loop-opening pose at f22.

keyPoses.role: stride A extreme and highest pelvis point of the cycle
mid-cycle pose with the pelvis at its leftmost point
stride B extreme with shoulder and leg rotation excursions clustered around this frame

weightTransfer: Pelvis translation shows a small lateral shift combined with vertical bob across the two half-strides: the pelvis rises to its maximum height at f5, reaches its leftmost point at f11, reverses toward the right during the second half of the cycle, reaches both its rightmost and lowest point at f20, and returns near the loop-opening state by f22. This supports pelvis weight shift, but not an exact planted/support foot or frame-level foot-contact assignment.
bodyMechanics: The motion coordinates the alternating lower-body cycle with trunk and arm counter-motion. A leg-rotation cluster reaches an extreme at f5, the leg configuration transitions toward the opposite half-cycle around f11, Chest has its largest frame-to-frame rotation change at f13, Spine at f14, hips/spine/chest and upper arms reach a large excursion region relative to f0 at f15, and shoulders together with a leg-rotation cluster reach a large excursion region at f16. Because torso and arm extrema cluster closely across f13-f16, no rigid proximal-to-distal sequence is asserted.

recommended: pelvis vertical bob and lateral shift in a running cycle
torso and arm counter-motion coordinated with the stride
notRecommendedAsPrimary: frame-level foot-contact timing without additional world-space foot or contact data
ground-reaction force or real load-distribution analysis
